title: Give the idea a name after the learner has met it
before: The learner has seen a concrete relationship.
after: A new term names something recognizable.
sequence: Introduce the conventional name with its scope.

source.title: Grant Sanderson — advice for making explanations
source.locator: FAQ: advice for making math videos

observation: Sanderson warns that pedagogical ordering can differ from the order in which definitions are normally presented.
interpretation: A name should compress an idea the learner has already encountered.
example: After seeing work overlap, introduce concurrency as the name for that overlap.
avoid: Replacing a missing explanation with a glossary.
Introducing several dependent terms at once.
check: Can the learner point to an instance of the named idea?
